title: Tower derived limit core
statement: Let A be an abelian category with exact countable products, enough injectives and derived category D(A) [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with any instance of countable products on D(A). For a K-injective complex I of inverse systems and an isomorphism of its represented tower with (K,f), there is a limit cone of I.asFunctor whose image under Q is a derived limit [def-weil-derived-limit] of (K,f).

proof.text: For (3), for each $n$ the functor $\lambda_n:\mathcal A\to\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ sending $X$ to the tower equal to $X$ at levels $m\le n$ with identity transitions and $0$ at levels $m>n$ is exact and left adjoint to evaluation $\operatorname{ev}_n$ (a map $\lambda_nX\to Y_\bullet$ is determined by its level-$n$ component $X\to Y_n$), so [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] makes each $\operatorname{ev}_n(I_\bullet)$ K-injective. By [lem-pc-ringed-space-product-kinjective] (a general abelian category, applied to the countable index set of levels, whose termwise products exist by hypothesis) the termwise product $P=\prod_n\operatorname{ev}_n(I_\bullet)$ is K-injective and represents $\prod_nK_n$ in $D(\mathcal A)$ with the projections, as also given by Step 2; the chain map $1-s:P\to P$ satisfies $\mathrm{pr}_n\circ(1-s)=\mathrm{pr}_n-f_n\circ\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}$, so it represents the transition endomorphism of [def-weil-derived-limit].

The mapping cone of the chain map $1-s:P\to P$ gives the distinguished cone triangle $P\xrightarrow{1-s}P\to\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)\to P[1]$ of $D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; rotating it back by TR2 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] gives a distinguished triangle $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]\to P\xrightarrow{1-s}P\to\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)$, so by Step 3 the object $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ is a derived limit of $(K_n,f_n)$ [def-weil-derived-limit]. By [lem-weil-derived-limit-roos-complex] the termwise inverse-limit complex $L=\varprojlim_nI_n$ is quasi-isomorphic to $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$, so it represents the same object of $D(\mathcal A)$, namely $R\varprojlim_nK_n$.

lean.statement:
theorem derivedCategory_towerLimit_core
    (A : Type u) [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A]
    [HasCountableProducts A] [CountableAB4Star A]
    (hP : HasCountableProducts (DerivedCategory A)) :
    letI : HasCountableProducts (DerivedCategory A) := hP
    ∀ (_ : EnoughInjectives A)
      (I : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ℤ) [I.IsKInjective]
      (K : ℕ → DerivedCategory A) (f : ∀ n : ℕ, K (n + 1) ⟶ K n)
      (_e : I.asFunctor ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ≅ Functor.ofOpSequence f),
      ∃ c : Cone I.asFunctor, Nonempty (IsLimit c) ∧
        IsDerivedLimit f (DerivedCategory.Q.obj c.pt)
